items.bold: IRAN SEIZED TWO SHIPS + ATTACKED THIRD on April 22 — first seizures since Feb 28.
items.text: In the most significant West Asia War naval escalation since the Touska seizure (April 19), the IRGC attacked and seized multiple vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on April 22 — just hours after Trump announced the indefinite ceasefire extension. NPR confirmed three ships were attacked. Time confirmed this is "the first time Tehran has seized ships since the start of the war on Feb. 28." The three vessels: (1) Epaminondas (Greek-owned cargo ship) — IRGC gunboat attacked with gunfire and rocket-propelled grenades near coast of Oman, causing significant bridge damage. Ship had been given permission to cross. UKMTO first report: 5:47 AM London time, 15 miles NE of Oman. (2) MSC Francesca — targeted off coast of Iran, instructed to drop anchor, hull and accommodation damage. Iran said it was "seized." (3) Euphoria — targeted by IRGC, briefly "stranded" on Iranian coast, later found undamaged and resumed sailing. No injuries reported in any of the three incidents. IRGC stated the seizures were "in response to the US capture of the Iranian commercial vessel" — direct retaliation for the Touska seizure.

items.bold: TRUMP gave Iran 3-5 DAYS — new soft deadline ~April 25-27 for talks or resumed attacks.
items.text: Wikipedia ceasefire article (confirmed April 22): "US officials said that Trump has given Iran three to five days to engage in negotiations and resolve alleged infringement within the government before resuming attacks." This creates a new soft deadline: approximately April 25-27. Trump also posted on Truth Social: "Iran is collapsing financially! Starving for cash! Losing $500M a day. Military and Police complaining they are not getting paid. SOS!!!" And separately: "Iran doesn't want the Strait of Hormuz closed, they want it open so they can make $500M a day." items.bold: 30-COUNTRY MILITARY CONFERENCE at UK Northwood base — multinational Hormuz force planning.
items.text: UK and France hosted military planners from 30+ countries at the UK's Permanent Joint Headquarters in Northwood, north London — a two-day conference (April 22-23) to plan a multinational mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. NPR and CNN confirmed. The conference will cover military capabilities, command and control structures, and deployment plans. Crucially: any plan will only take effect "as soon as conditions permit, following a sustainable ceasefire agreement." This is not a war-fighting conference — it is planning for the post-ceasefire reopening. The UK defence ministry said it was the latest step after a virtual summit with 51 countries hosted by UK PM Starmer and French President Macron the previous Friday. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas: "Freedom of navigation is non-negotiable." EU also widening sanctions on Tehran.

items.bold: Lufthansa cut 20,000 flights. United Airlines profits below estimates. EU: 6 weeks jet fuel.

United Airlines has also been impacted, with Reuters reporting the carrier had "forecast second-quarter and full-year profits below Wall Street estimates" due to fuel costs. The IEA head earlier warned Europe has "maybe six weeks or so" of jet fuel remaining, with flight cancellations possible "soon." A UK poll shows 1 in 10 people are already stockpiling fuel. These airline industry developments signal the consumer economic impact of Hormuz closure is reaching daily life globally — Lufthansa alone serves tens of millions of passengers annually. assessment.body:
Thursday 8:30 AM IST. The West Asia War's stalemate just became an escalation.

WHAT HAPPENED ON APRIL 22
• Iran attacked and seized multiple vessels in Hormuz — first ship seizures since Feb 28
• EPAMINONDAS (Greek cargo): gunfire + rocket-propelled grenades, significant bridge damage — had prior permission to cross
• MSC FRANCESCA: targeted, instructed to anchor, hull damage — seized by Iran
• EUPHORIA: attacked, briefly stranded on Iranian coast — later resumed sailing undamaged
• No crew casualties — but no warning given before attacks (UKMTO confirmed)
• IRGC explicitly: "response to US capture of Iranian commercial vessel [Touska]"
• Brent briefly exceeded $100 — first time above $100 since April 8 ceasefire

THE TIT-FOR-TAT PATTERN
• April 19: USS Spruance seized TOUSKA (Iranian) — blew hole in engine room
• April 21: US seized M/T TIFANI in Indian Ocean
• April 22: Iran seized MSC FRANCESCA + EPAMINONDAS (non-Iranian)
• April 22: Trump gives Iran 3-5 days (~April 25-27) or strikes resume
• Each action invites retaliation — the cycle is accelerating

THE NEW 3-5 DAY WINDOW
• US officials: Trump gave Iran 3-5 days to engage in talks and resolve internal infighting
• New soft deadline: approximately April 25-27
• Trump simultaneously posting: "Iran is collapsing financially, losing $500M a day"
• Iran's IRGC responds by seizing ships — does not look like a government about to submit a proposal
• The Mojtaba Khamenei (new Supreme Leader, IRGC-aligned) structural constraint remains

30-COUNTRY CONFERENCE AT NORTHWOOD
• Military planners from 30+ nations meeting at UK Permanent Joint HQ
• Planning multinational Hormuz reopening force — post-ceasefire
• Will not act until "sustainable ceasefire achieved"
• EU widening sanctions on Tehran
• UK, France, US all coordinating on the military option

INDIA's SITUATION AT DAY 55
• Sensex 78,516 (-757) — IT worst, Iran risk re-priced
• Brent $99 — approaching critical OMC hike threshold of Rs 97-98
• Rupee ~94.50 and weakening
• 280 Indian seafarers in region. 8 Indian vessels. Op Urja Suraksha HIGH ALERT
• IMO: 20,000 mariners + 2,000 ships stranded in Gulf
• Infosys Q4 results TODAY — the domestic counterweight to geopolitical pressure
• Lufthansa + United = warning sign for IndiGo, Air India ATF cost impact

SCENARIO SHIFT — STALEMATE ENDING
• Iran submitting proposal in 3-5 days: 20%
• Stalemate continues (Trump extends again): 35%
• Strikes resume after deadline: 25%
• Uncontrolled escalation (Iran attacks US asset): 20%

VERDICT: The stalemate is over. Iran's seizure of two ships was the IRGC's reply to the Touska seizure — a deliberate escalation inside the ceasefire. Trump's 3-5 day ultimatum is the tightest pressure point since the indefinite extension was announced. India's markets open this morning with Brent at $99, a Sensex that fell 757 points yesterday, and Infosys results due today. The next 72 hours will determine whether the West Asia War enters its most dangerous phase since February 28.
